_about: A relevance benchmark for Firmo search.
Each case is a topic a student might actually type, paired with papers a
human judged squarely on-topic for it. Those papers are the ground truth: a
run scores by how many of them Firmo surfaces, and how high.
Every reference here was resolved against a real index before being added,
by verify_benchmark.py. That check matters more than it sounds: a first
draft of this file was written from memory and a third of the DOIs were
wrong, one of them pointing at an entirely different paper. The same is true
of titles, and worse, because a title remembered slightly wrong can never be
matched and reports itself as a retrieval failure forever. A benchmark with
bad ground truth is not a weak benchmark, it is confident nonsense.
ALWAYS run verify_benchmark.py after editing this file.
Fields:
must_find         DOIs of papers a good search has to return.
must_find_titles  Titles, for papers with no CrossRef DOI. arXiv registers
with DataCite, and books and working papers are often in
neither, so an arXiv-only paper can never be matched by
DOI and would otherwise score as a permanent miss. The
verifier checks these against CrossRef and then OpenAlex,
which does index books and preprints.
off_topic_terms   Words that signal the wrong sense of an ambiguous query.
Counted separately because that failure (armed conflict
for high-conflict divorce) is the one semantic ranking
was introduced to fix. Several cases exist only to test
it: attention-psychology against the transformer paper,
depression-economics against clinical depression,
memory-computing against human memory.
Coverage: 32 cases across 19 disciplines, spread deliberately across the
question shapes the product recognises - degree, mechanism, comparison,
enumeration, interpretive, conditional - because ranking that works on
"does X cause Y" can quietly fail on "what is new historicism", and the
humanities half of the set is what catches it.
